body:
From crash to war

In 1933, one American worker in four had no job. Banks had failed by the thousands, and families lost their savings overnight. Franklin D. Roosevelt promised "action, and action now," and his New Deal changed what Americans expected from their national government. Then, in December 1941, the country entered the largest war in history.

In this unit you will read the Depression in numbers, analyze how Roosevelt defined freedom, investigate the incarceration of about 120,000 people of Japanese ancestry, and argue whether the New Deal ended the Depression.

Watch our two semester threads come together. The government's role in the economy grows more in these twelve years than in any other period. And the question of who receives the full rights of citizenship is tested again in wartime, as it was in 1918.

Key terms: unemployment rate, bank run, New Deal, relief, recovery, reform, Social Security, deficit spending, internment, incarceration.
title: Fear Itself
